newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel falls against dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel falls against dollar, basket.

text.p: The shekel weakened against the dollar and the basket of key foreign currencies on Wednesday as a result of growing demand for dollars from the business sector, dealers said.

"The business sector has started closing positions before the end of the year," said Zahi Elias, a trader at Bank Leumi. "Investors are repaying dollar-linked loans and others are taking profits following the recent rise of the shekel."
He said inter-bank trading was also active, with the banks also converting shekels into dollars.

The shekel's softening marks a reversal after it gained earlier in the week in response to the Bank of Israel's announcement Monday that it was holding short-term interest rates unchanged at 15.2 percent for December.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2520 shekels against 3.2420 on Tuesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, closed at 3.6509 shekels against 3.6376 on Tuesday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.8704 shekels per 100 yen against 2.8770 on Tuesday and against the mark at 2.1323 shekels against 2.1232 on Tuesday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.2510 shekels.
